chunks: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Asim ibn Humayd, who said:

I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding what they narrate about the Vision [of God], and he said: The sun is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Throne [al-Kursi], and the Throne is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Empyrean [al-Arsh], and the Empyrean is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Veil [al-Hijab], and the Veil is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Cover [al-Sitr]. So if they are truthful, let them fill their eyes with the sun, with no cloud before it.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for the vision of God in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs a cosmological analogy of light intensity to address the debate on 'Ru'yah' (Vision of God), asserting that the sun is but a minute fraction of the light of the Throne and beyond. This hierarchy implies that if humans can endure the sun's radiance, they are capable of beholding the Divine Light in the afterlife, thereby supporting the possibility of visual perception of God. This narration is central to the Shia scholarly tradition in reconciling the physical limitations of human sight with the metaphysical reality of divine manifestation.
